Permission Receipts in the app vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume access-receipt features cover storefront language. In-app permission logging and App Store Connect actually separate per-access transparency from product-page copy:

  • Permission Receipts (权限回执 / 访问回执) — per-access permission-use receipts your app surfaces when camera, microphone, contacts, location, photos, or other sensitive permissions are exercised. Access-receipt cards, permission-use timelines, and "see when this app used your mic" UX. Runtime app behavior — does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • Access receipt timelines (权限使用记录) — chronological permission-use records buyers review inside your app. Listing copy may reference 权限使用记录 when your gallery shows those timelines — engineering the log is separate from Connect metadata.
  • Privacy manifests and required-reason APIs — developer-side declarations in the binary. Engineering inside Xcode — not listing rewrite.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Permission Receipts marketing on your US gallery.

An app that ships Permission Receipts in the binary and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe access-receipt and permission-use transparency on the store page in zh-Hans, not how you implement permission logging in code.

Permission Receipts–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Permission Receipts listings use vocabulary general App Privacy Report guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate access-receipt claims — not a literal paste of US marketing:

权限回执 vs 访问回执 vs 权限使用记录

US pages say "Permission Receipt", "Access Receipt", or "Permission Use Record." China storefront copy often uses 权限回执 for permission receipt badge callouts, 访问回执 when gallery frames emphasize access-receipt transparency per permission exercise, and 权限使用记录 when marketing chronological permission-use timelines. AppLocale aligns phrasing with each screenshot frame — not one blanket term for every overlay.

Per-access receipts vs App Privacy Report dashboards

Permission Receipts (权限回执) show when your app exercised a specific permission — camera, microphone, contacts, location, photos. App Privacy Report (App隐私报告) is a system Settings dashboard summarizing activity across apps with network-activity charts. Listing caption lines should match the surface your screenshot shows — a permission receipt card is not a Network Activity domain frequency list.

Camera, microphone, contacts, location, and photos vocabulary

Access-receipt timelines name specific permission types — 摄像头权限, 麦克风权限, 通讯录权限, 位置权限, 照片权限. Listing caption lines should match the permission your screenshot highlights. A microphone access receipt is not a camera-permission onboarding sheet and not an ATT tracking prompt.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need access-receipt search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 权限回执 and 访问回执 signal different intent from App Privacy Report keywords like 隐私报告 or 网络活动.

Screenshot captions on Permission Receipts frames

Gallery frames that show permission receipt cards or access-receipt timelines need one-line zh-Hans captions — "查看应用何时使用麦克风权限" not "Permission Receipt" burned into the product page story alone.

FAQ

What are Permission Receipts and why do they matter for listing copy?

Permission Receipts are per-access permission-use receipts — access-receipt transparency when an app exercises camera, microphone, contacts, location, photos, or other sensitive permissions. Marketing those surfaces on your en-US page does not auto-fill a zh-Hans localization row.

Are Permission Receipts the same as App Privacy Report?

No. App Privacy Report is the on-device Settings dashboard under Privacy & Security showing cross-app App Activity and Network Activity charts. Permission Receipts are per-access access-receipt UX when your app exercises a specific permission. See our App Privacy Report listing guide for dashboard scope — not Permission Receipts screenshot marketing.

Are Permission Receipts the same as Privacy Nutrition Labels?

No. Privacy Nutrition Labels are App Store Connect questionnaire disclosures for the Privacy Details panel. Permission Receipts are access-receipt transparency when permissions are exercised. See our privacy nutrition labels listing guide for Connect filing scope.
